description: issue #864: the Core-only half of the value-position rule, and the byte-identical twin of `block-heads-not-values`. A profile word has no structural role while its profile is inactive (`spec/tooling.md:30`'s "while their profile is active"), so in VALUE position a Core-only program sees four names nothing in THIS program declares, which is `ol-unknown-command` (`spec/tooling.md:181`), not the wrong-position `ol-bad-token` its twin reports for the very same bytes. That contrast is the whole point of the pair: it pins issue #864's rule as PROFILE-GATED rather than a blanket rejection, which is what keeps `ol-bad-token` scoped to a word the ACTIVE profile gives a structural role. The DECLARATION axis is the opposite and is pinned by the pair `block-heads-free-core-only` / `block-heads-reserved-under-profile`: since issue #841 a Core-only `define every` raises `ol-reserved-word` (`spec/grammar.md:408`). This fixture asserts a NAME-visibility outcome, not a declaration one, which is why #841 had nothing here to invalidate. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static legality only and does not execute.
